response.answer: Dr. Patrick Roberts is a leading researcher on ancient composite bow technology, reassessing its origins and spread. His 2020 study published in *Science Advances* revealed the earliest use of bow-and-arrow technology outside Africa. His work highlights the global spread of material culture innovations.

results.title: Discovery of Oldest Bow and Arrow Technology in Eurasia
results.content: In this new study, published in *Science Advances*, an international team of researchers from the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History (MPI-SHH) in Germany, Griffith University in Australia and the Department of Archaeology, Government of Sri Lanka, present evidence for the earliest use of bow-and-arrow technologies by humans anywhere outside of Africa. As co-author of the new study, Patrick Roberts of the MPI-SHH argues that “this traditional focus has meant that other parts of Africa, Asia, Australasia, and the Americas have often been side-lined in discussions of the origins of material culture, such as novel projectile hunting methods or cultural innovations associated with our species.” Nevertheless, the last twenty years have highlighted how Pleistocene humans occupied and adapted to a variety of extreme environments as they migrated beyond Africa, including deserts, high-altitude settings and tropical rainforests such as those of Sri Lanka.
